full_query: The yeast infection is not transferable?
sentences: Yeast infections are typically not transferable from one person to another through casual contact, such as hugging, kissing, or sharing personal items
However, there are some exceptions and considerations to note
Yeast infections are caused by a fungus called Candida, which is a normal inhabitant of the human body
In most cases, Candida exists in balance with other microorganisms on the skin and mucous membranes, but when the balance is disrupted, it can lead to an overgrowth and infection
While it is rare, it is possible for a yeast infection to be transmitted through sexual contact, particularly if one partner has a weakened immune system or is taking antibiotics
This is because Candida can be present in the genital area and can be transmitted through skin-to-skin contact
It's also worth noting that Candida can be spread through sharing personal items, such as towels or clothing, that have come into contact with an infected person's bodily fluids
However, this is not a common mode of transmission
In general, yeast infections are not contagious in the classical sense and do not spread from person to person through casual contact
